blocks.text: The module documentation explains which states retain buffers, how start/resume/end/cancel/purge work, and how stale-run sweeping fails closed.
blocks.title: Run and buffer lifecycle contract

blocks.text: Fixed-text exceptions cover resume, validation, cleanup, and ended-run cases. Resumed reports replay/rebuild status, while SweepReport contains only counts.
blocks.title: Errors and result records

blocks.text: Protocol loading and tolerant envelope validation protect start/resume state. Helpers split state from history, clear guard rails, and delete buffers while preserving cleanup failures.
blocks.title: Validation and cleanup helpers

blocks.text: start_run validates and records a created run before creating its buffer. resume_run enforces ownership and terminal rules, while _attach replays a live buffer or rebuilds it from validated device state.
blocks.title: Start and resume attachment

blocks.text: pause_run keeps the buffer for later resume. end_run, cancel_run, and purge_run transition or verify terminal state, then remove buffers and run-guard rails.
blocks.title: Pause and terminal operations

blocks.text: PgSweepStore performs the documented trusted cross-account read. _sweep_page translates failures, and _as_utc normalizes sweep time input.
blocks.title: Paged stale-run reads

blocks.text: expire_stale pages idle open rows and delegates each to _sweep_one. A live buffer is kept, a corrupt one is counted unreadable, and an absent buffer is transitioned to expired and cleaned.
blocks.title: Fail-closed stale sweep

gotchas: A cleanup failure means the run is already terminal and raises CleanupIncomplete.
Sweep stops without expiring more when liveness cannot be determined.
how_it_works: Creates, resumes, pauses, ends, cancels, and purges runs
Deletes buffers and guard rails for terminal runs
Pages idle rows and expires only runs with absent buffers
purpose: The run manager keeps the SQL run state and Redis buffer lifecycle consistent. It validates start/resume payloads, creates or rebuilds buffers, transitions paused and terminal states, clears run-guard rails, and sweeps idle open runs whose buffers have disappeared.
summary: Coordinates persistent run rows with encrypted conversation buffers, resume, cleanup, and stale-run expiry.
